whatWasWrong.finding: filing-instructions.md told the participant, in the record's own voice, that the record 'does not record a fee-waiver treatment'. rules.feeWaiver exists and reads 'not applicable; no fee is identified.' loadControllingRecord() captured fees, service, notarization and participantSignature and never opened feeWaiver, so nothing in the build reached the node the sentence described. Confirmed independently before it was acted on: `grep -n 'RECORD\.\(fees\|service\|notarization\|participantSignature\|clerkDuties\)'` over the builder returned NOTHING — all five loaded fields were unused by every document, and the whole of filing-instructions.md was lines.push() literals.

The same file's second negative claim — 'The record does not state a service deadline or a filing deadline' — was also a literal asserted by a document that had not read the node. It happens to be true of rules, but it was true by luck rather than by measurement, and the record's waitingPeriods node (the six-month gate that is the whole eligibility test of this route) was never read at all.

whatWasDone.change: A new auditDeclaredComponents() reads the record's component rows and decides, per component, what this build delivers for it and what the component's own note promises that this build does not. The promised instrument is found by testing the note's own words (/\bcertificate\b/), not by a list typed in the builder, so a note that grows a second promise is caught the same way. The result reaches four places at once: build-findings.json (findingCount is now 1, with the full component set and the verbatim note); product-wiring.json (binding.instrumentKinds now lists only ['primary_filing'], what this family actually delivers, with declaredComponentsNotDeliveredInFull and instrumentKindsDeclaredByTheRecordButNotDeliveredHere carrying the rest and the reason); filing-instructions.md (a participant-facing section 'What this packet does not contain'); and this lane's counters.
whatWasDone.whyTheCertificateWasNotBuilt: Because building it would have required inventing. Measured, not assumed: (1) NO FORM. This family binds exactly one binary — AOC-275.18 Rev. 1-16, one page, 16 AcroForm fields, sha256 b3d8278a…cb51 — and its extracted page text contains the word 'certificate' nowhere. What it prints instead is the CLERK's distribution list ('Copies to: Court file / Petitioner / Respondent') inside the NOTIFICATION OF EXPUNGEMENT HEARING block, above a '_____ Clerk' and 'By: _____ D.C.' signature pair. The only other form the record names, AOC-275.19, was never retrieved and is itself carried as a release blocker in unresolvedQuestions[1]. (2) NO FACTS. A certificate recites who was served, at what address, by what means and on what date. The petitioner's name and address is the third person this packet deliberately leaves blank throughout — that withholding is the family's own settled position and VF24 re-confirmed zero ink in that block. The hearing date is set by the clerk AFTER filing (rules.notice: 'The clerk completes the notification-of-hearing section on the form and creates the scheduled event.'), and the mailing date is after that. A certificate reciting facts nobody holds is a fabricated service record on a sworn filing. The builder now asserts the 'no form' half at build time: if a future revision of AOC-275.18 ever prints a certificate, the build stops and the question is decided again rather than inherited.
